Package dev.px.core.render

Interface Render2D

public interface Render2D
The pluggable 2D drawing backend.

Implement this once per rendering library and Core, the GUI, and every HUD element draw through it unchanged. NanoVG, Skija, and legacy immediate-mode OpenGL all fit; nothing here assumes a graphics API.

Coordinates are in scaled screen space with the origin at the top left, the same space the game reports mouse positions in. The backend is responsible for converting to whatever its library wants.

Call sites use the Render facade rather than this interface. Only the adapter that installs a backend ever sees it.

  • Method Details

    • beginFrame

      void beginFrame(float width, float height, float scale)
      Opens a frame. Called once before any drawing each time the client renders.

      Retained-mode libraries need this to begin a scene and to learn the current framebuffer size; an immediate-mode backend can push GL state here and pop it in endFrame().

      Parameters:
      width - scaled screen width
      height - scaled screen height
      scale - pixels per scaled unit, for backends that rasterise at native resolution

      void textShadowed(Font font, String value, float x, float y, Color color, Color shadowColor)
      Draws text with a drop shadow.

      Separate from text(dev.px.core.render.font.Font, java.lang.String, float, float, dev.px.core.render.Color) because backends implement it very differently: a blur-capable library does it properly, while a legacy backend draws the string twice.

    • blur

      void blur(float x, float y, float width, float height, float radius)
      Blurs what is already on screen within the given bounds.

      Backends that cannot blur should leave the region untouched rather than approximating it with a flat fill, so the caller can detect the difference through supportsBlur().
